title: get-media-init acknowledgements arriving after stop() rebuild a MediaSource and hijack the video element
test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-092: an init answer that arrives after stop() leaves a stopped player alone', 'VAL-092: a reset recovery answer that arrives after stop() leaves a stopped player alone', 'VAL-092: an init answer from before stop() is ignored by the same player started again' and 'VAL-092: an init answer that a newer request has replaced is ignored'
proof: On the unchanged player all four tests failed because a late successful get-media-init answer after stop() (or from before stop(), or from a replaced request) built a MediaSource: 'no MediaSource is built after stop()' expected 0, actual 1 (first test); expected 1, actual 2 (reset recovery test); the restart test and the newer-request test failed the same way (expected 0, actual 1: the older answer, delivered after the timeout had sent a newer request, built a MediaSource). The tests stop at that first failing assertion on the unchanged code; their second half (a late failed answer after stop(), which on the unchanged code reaches handleError for a reset recovery) passes only with the fix. After the fix all pass: requestCurrentInit now counts requests in initRequestEpoch and its answer returns early when state is 'stopped' or the epoch moved on; stop() and handleError() also move the epoch on; the sourceopen handler returns early when the player is stopped or its MediaSource is no longer the current one.

title: resetAndRequestInit recovery fails permanently on one unavailable response and can hang with no timeout
test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-093: reset recovery retries an init segment that is not available yet', 'VAL-093: reset recovery whose answer never arrives retries, then reports one error' and 'VAL-093: stop() during reset recovery clears the retry and timeout timers'
proof: On the unchanged player, one {success:false} answer to the reset's get-media-init called handleError at once: the first test failed with errors ['Failed to recover — init segment unavailable'] where [] was expected, and the stop() test failed the same way. With the answer never delivered, the second test failed at its first check (expected 1 fallback-consume-start after 15 s, actual 0): no init timeout was armed, so the player stayed in 'buffering' with no retry and no error. After the fix resetAndRequestInit arms the init timeout, resets the retry budget and goes through requestCurrentInit, so an unavailable answer is retried every 2 s (scheduleInitRetry) and a missing one runs into the timeout, which retries three times and then reports one error, 'Relay init segment did not arrive in time'. The tests also show success after one unavailable answer, a single terminal error, no retry after it, and that stop() leaves no retry or timeout timer.
